title: TlsIntermediates
description: Public CA intermediate certificates that some official portals leave out of their TLS handshake. Each one completes a chain to a root the runtime already trusts; none is ever a trust anchor of its own. The checker verifies every entry before installing it, so a manifest that has gone stale stops a run instead of weakening it.

purpose.description: Why this file exists, for whoever finds it without the surrounding context.

certificates.description: One entry per intermediate. A portal that serves a complete chain needs none.

intermediate.title: Intermediate
intermediate.description: One public intermediate certificate, pinned by fingerprint and traceable to the certificate authority that publishes it.

subject.description: The distinguished name of the certificate, comma-separated, as a reader would recognise it.

issuer.description: The root that issued it, which has to be one the runtime already trusts. Recorded so the chain this entry completes is readable without parsing the certificate.

validTo.description: When the certificate expires, exactly as the certificate states it. Documentation only: the expiry is checked against the certificate itself, never against this field.

sha256Fingerprint.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint, uppercase and colon-separated. The certificate is rejected unless it matches, which is what makes this a pin rather than a bundled file.

source.description: The certificate authority's own address for this certificate, so anybody can download it and compare the fingerprint. Certificate authorities publish these over plain HTTP, which is safe here precisely because the fingerprint is pinned.

servedIncompleteBy.description: The hosts observed serving a chain that needs this intermediate. It says why the entry is here, and an entry nobody needs can be removed.

items.description: A hostname, as it appears in the cited source URLs.

addedOn.description: The date this entry was added, so an intermediate nobody has needed for years can be reconsidered.
